setlist.title: It's All Over Now, Baby Blue

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Little Red Rooster** (2 reviews): Band played tight, extended jams; Phil redirected crowd applause to the drummers; Venue exploded at 6:40 minutes; Jerry stayed bouncy and funky throughout [21][29]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (1 review): Review calls the Lovelight performance amazing, noting the show is a 1987 highlight [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1987-04-10.sbd.unknown.mtownshend.102188.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 135 min; rated 1.33/5 by 3 [1]
- **gd1987-04-10.167472.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 134 min [7]
- **gd87-04-10.nak.braverman.10537.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 129 min; rated 4.25/5 by 16 [13]. Said about its sound: Audio is described as a little hollow, though jams and Red Rooster are strong; Recording quality is criticized as muddy, distant, and having level issues [24][25]
- **gd1987-04-10.nak300.gidley.andrewf.93385.sbeok.flac16**: audience recording; 21 songs; 133 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [2]

## Around the show

- Listener sat on aisle steps post-show, muttering about the music's unique sound [19]
- Phil emerged with a Frankenstein walk, then screamed "You guessed it!" into the mic [20]
- Local women guarding doors were hysterical, caught in the vortex of the energy [30]
- Show was mellower than the previous night, but much better than the final run [28]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1987-04-10.sbd.unknown.mtownshend.102188.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by mtownsend; source: SBD Unknown [1]
- **gd1987-04-10.167472.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Michael Hessberg; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Michael Hessberg's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser ME-80 mics > Sony D5M [7]
- **gd87-04-10.nak.braverman.10537.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Cassette (Nakamichi 300/Sony D5) [13]
- **gd1987-04-10.nak300.gidley.andrewf.93385.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Ted Gidley; transferred by Andrew F.; source: OTS AUD: Nakamichi CM300's w/CP4 shotguns > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell MX-90's, with no Dolby. [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Robbi Cohn: [1987-04-09 UIC Pavilion, Chicago, IL, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1987-04-09-uic-pavilion-chicago-il-usa/) [32]
- Poster by Ron Delany Grateful Dead: [1987-04-11 UIC Pavilion, Chicago, IL, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1987-04-11-uic-pavilion-chicago-il-usa/) [33]
- Poster by Ron Delany Grateful Dead: [1987-04-10 UIC Pavilion, Chicago, IL, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1987-04-10-uic-pavilion-chicago-il-usa/) [34]

facts.lineage: The Master Cassettes were played back with Azimuth adjustment and Dolby B decoding on a Nakamichi CD1 into a Korg MR1000 at DSF 1 bit 5.6MHz. Subsequent conversion to 24/96 AIFF done via Korg Audiogate software. Redbook CDR standard 16/44.1 files were created using Bias Peak, Izotope Ozone's MBIT+ (for all dithering), and Weiss Saracon SRC (all sample rate conversions).
facts.source: 2 Nakamichi CM100/CP4s>Nakamichi 550 w/Maxell XLIIS 90 cassettes. Dolby B was used on the Master Cassettes. Sec. 109 Row U Seat 17 8 ft. stand.
